const ans = `FINAL ANSWER (ideation_2) — CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN

IDEA: CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN
TITLE: Capacity-frozen, successor-curvature-field Poincare assignment for the RQ-VAE, with code radius untouched by construction
MOTIVATION: The prior round proved the curvature signal tracks SID quality (Spearman -0.20) but spent it on the per-level code radius rho_l, collapsing the codebook (2/13/56 support, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, recall 0.041888). Curvature and resolution were competing for the same scalar. The fix is to change the currency: curvature may only decide WHICH item occupies WHICH code, never how much of the ball a code occupies.
NOVELTY: Unlike CURVALLOC (curvature->c_l and rho_l), BRad-RQ (rank/radial assignment), CURVCTRL-SID (prefix score -> level temperature), poincare-frechet (curved codebook update), and unlike a behaviour-weighted Sinkhorn with an additive Euclidean cost, behaviour here is not a weight: it IS the local curvature of the distance, c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), and the transport column marginals are frozen to the Euclidean nearest-code counts, so curvature is structurally incapable of changing code usage.
CHANGE: Replaces the per-level nearest-code step by a curvature-field, capacity-frozen optimal-transport assignment in which each item-code pair has its own Poincare sectional curvature, set by the fraction of the item's training successors already sitting in that code's community.
SPECIFICATION: Per level l: map residual and codes into a Poincare ball with per-level curvature c_l (from the standardised behaviour-graph curvature profile), compute pair cost C_ik = d_{c_ik}(psi(z_i),psi(v_k)) with c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), solve a Sinkhorn plan P whose row sums are 1 and whose column sums are exactly the Euclidean nearest-code counts u_k of the same batch, take the code as argmax_k P_ik with straight-through gradient through the soft code, and recurse on the residual. Column capacities = Euclidean counts is the resolution guarantee: the per-level usage multiset, and therefore the exported support, is exactly the Euclidean one.
COST: Added ~108M MAC/step at the frozen scale (B=1023, K=256, d=64, J=10: 3*B*K*d for the curved cost matrix, 3*B*K*d for the Euclidean capacity pass, 3*B*K*J for Sinkhorn) ~0.22 GFLOP/step, i.e. ~1.0-1.8x the ~120M MAC RQ-VAE step; 72,000 steps -> ~1.6e13 added FLOPs, ~10-40 min extra on four cards including launch overhead. Curvature schedule (60 recomputations x 3 levels x <=256-node exact ORC) < 1 min. For K=256 per level (consistent with 247/7414/20223) this is the budget; if a level used K=4096 the per-step MAC grows 16x for that level.
HYPOTHESIS: If the level-l prefix of an item should coincide with the level-l prefix its training successors already occupy, then letting curvature pull the assignment toward successor codes while capacity forbids resolution loss should raise prefix sharing along transitions and lift Stage3 test_recall@10 from 0.055537 above 0.065, with the SID support unchanged and 5-40% of level-1 codes permuted relative to geometry-off.
RISKS: the curvature carrier is a 3-vector (low bandwidth); a_ik from Euclidean successor codes may be noisy early and act as a random permutation; Sinkhorn temperature from the measured gap can be unstable in early epochs; capacity matching limits codebook adaptation; cross-level collisions may rise even with per-level support preserved; curvature could still act as a mild regulariser with <1% assignment change.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transitions, aggregated as each item's top-M training successor set plus the level-l community curvature of the training transition quotient graph.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the TRAIN split only: scan each user's consecutive interactions, count item->item transitions, keep the top M=20 successors S(i) per item (ties by item id) in a cached sparse matrix; per level, euc_l(j) = argmin_k ||z_j^l - v_k|| for all 24556 training items, recomputed identically at each epoch from the current codebook; a_ik = (1/|S(i)|)*sum_{j in S(i)} 1[euc_l(j)=k] in [0,1]. Curvature profile: nodes = the K_l codes used at level l, edge weight w_kk' = number of training transitions u->v with euc_l(u)=k, euc_l(v)=k'; Ollivier-Ricci curvature kappa(k,k') = 1 - W1(m_k,m_k')/d_G(k,k') with m_k = 0.5*delta_k + 0.5*sum_k' (w_kk'/deg k) delta_k', exact OT on <=256 nodes; kappa_l = transition-weighted edge mean; 200 member-shuffles preserving community sizes give mu_l, sigma_l; kappa_hat_l = clip((kappa_l-mu_l)/max(sigma_l,1e-6), -2, 2); delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l' kappa_hat_l'. Recompute every 50 epochs under no_grad.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Every transition, successor set, community size, curvature, null sample, capacity count and code table is built from training interactions and the training item universe only. Validation/test interactions are never tokenised, never counted in w_kk', never used for a_ik or u_k. The curvature profile is computed offline before launch, written to a file and read identically by all ranks, so no validation pass can influence SID construction; the export uses only train-fitted codebooks.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball distance with Mobius addition and a per-pair negative sectional curvature -c_ik, c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), c_l = clamp(exp(-delta_l/2), 0.25, 4.0), c_0 = 1 dimensionless: d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-u) (+) c v||). Curvature is fixed/scheduled, not trained.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual quantizer's assignment step at all three levels, and in the gradient that flows through the straight-through soft plan to the encoder and codebook; not in the code radius, not in the decoder, not the latent scale.
COUPLING PATH: a_ik (training successors' codes) sets the local curvature c_ik of the distance that prices item i against code k; the same distance forms the cost matrix of a transport whose marginals are frozen to the Euclidean counts, so the transport plan, the code, the residual and the next level's assignment all depend jointly on the behaviour affinity and the curved metric. Removing behaviour makes c_ik uniform (no successor channel); removing geometry makes the cost Euclidean and the affinity has no channel at all, so the plan collapses to the Euclidean assignment.
COUPLING EQUATION: C_ik = d_{c_l * exp(-a_ik)}( psi(z_i^l), psi(v_k) ), with a_ik = (1/|S(i)|) sum_{j in S(i)} 1[euc_l(j)=k] and c_l = exp(-delta_l/2).
OBSERVABLES: (1) fraction of items whose level-l code differs from the geometry-off assignment (target 5-40%; <1% means the curvature is inert); (2) exact equality of the per-level usage multiset with the Euclidean counts, logged every step; (3) exported support, which must be >= the same-run Euclidean support and is expected to stay at or above 247 level-1 codes / 7414 prefixes / 20223 three-token SIDs; (4) collision rate and L1 positive/negative hit rates must stay near the frozen baseline rather than 0.998/0.982/0.980; (5) successor prefix hit rate, the fraction of training transitions with code_l(u)=code_l(v), should rise above the geometry-off run; (6) Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 against the frozen 0.055537.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: config flag behaviour_off sets a_ik = 0 for all pairs and delta_l = 0, so c_ik = 1 for every level; the cost is a uniform-curvature Poincare distance and the capacity-frozen Sinkhorn is otherwise unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: config flag geometry_off sets C_ik = ||z_i^l - v_k|| (Euclidean limit); because the column capacities are exactly this assignment's own counts, the plan returns the Euclidean nearest-code assignment, so a_ik has no channel and the run is the plain RQ-VAE plus a no-op permutation.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full C_ik = d_{c_l*exp(-a_ik)}(psi(z_i),psi(v_k)) with capacity-frozen Sinkhorn and straight-through; this is the single trained arm (no arm is trained with the switches off in this round).
SPEC EQUATIONS: for l in 1..3: s_l = max(quantile_0.9({||z_i^l||} U {||v_k||}), 1e-8); psi(x) = (0.95/sqrt(c_l)) * tanh(||x||/(2*s_l)) * x/max(||x||,1e-12); a_ik as above (detached); c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik) (detached); C_ik = d_{c_ik}(psi(z_i),psi(v_k)); u_k = #{i: argmin_k'||z_i^l - v_k'|| = k}; tau = clamp(mean_i(C_i,(2)-C_i,(1)), 1e-3, 10); Kmat = exp(-C/tau); log-domain Sinkhorn j=1..10: f_i = -tau*logsumexp_k(-C_ik/tau + g_k); g_k = -tau*logsumexp_i(-C_ik/tau + f_i) + tau*log(u_k/B); P = softmax row/col normalised; repair column sums to u_k/B by largest remainder; c_ihat = argmax_k P_ik (ties by cost then code id); vbar_i = sum_k P_ik v_k; z_q = z_i + (v_{c_ihat} - z_i).detach() + (vbar_i - vbar_i.detach()); r_i^{l+1} = z_i^l - v_{c_ihat}. Loss unchanged from the RQ-VAE baseline (reconstruction + commitment); no new loss term and no new parameter.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: inputs z_i^l (batch x d), V_l (K x d), S(i) top-20 training successor lists, euc_l(.) over all training items, detached (c_l, s_l, tau); outputs per item a code c_ihat in 1..K, a quantized vector z_q, the residual r_i^{l+1}, and the plan P for the straight-through gradient.
SAFEGUARDS: psi maps into radius 0.95/sqrt(c_l) so sqrt(c_ik)||.|| <= 0.95 < 1 always; artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-6; Mobius denominator clamped to 1e-12; Sinkhorn in log domain with 10 iterations and largest-remainder repair of the column sums; tau clamped; deterministic tie-breaks; sigma_l floored at 1e-6 and delta_l=0 if the null is degenerate; c_l clamped to [0.25,4]; codes with u_k=0 are excluded from the plan exactly as in the Euclidean pass; s_l falls back to the previous step's value if the batch is degenerate; per-level usage-multiset equality is asserted and logged. Four-rank safety: the curvature profile is produced offline and read from a file by every rank, the Euclidean code table is recomputed identically on every rank from the replicated codebook after the DDP step, and any gather is an equal-shape all_gather on all ranks; no rank-0-only broadcast or export inside the training loop.
END IDEA`; const r = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: ans}); return r;

ABLATION BOTH ON: the full C_ik = d_{c_l*exp(-a_ik)}(psi(z_i), psi(v_k)) with capacity-frozen Sinkhorn and straight-through gradient; this is the single trained arm, and no arm is trained with the switches off in this round.
SPEC EQUATIONS: for l in 1..3: s_l = max(quantile_0.9({||z_i^l||} U {||v_k||}), 1e-8); psi(x) = (0.95/sqrt(c_l)) * tanh(||x||/(2*s_l)) * x/max(||x||,1e-12); a_ik as above, detached; c_ik = c_l*exp(-a_ik), detached; C_ik = d_{c_ik}(psi(z_i), psi(v_k)); u_k = #{i : argmin_k' ||z_i^l - v_k'|| = k}; tau = clamp(mean_i (C_i,(2) - C_i,(1)), 1e-3, 10); log-domain Sinkhorn for j=1..10, f_i = -tau*logsumexp_k(-C_ik/tau + g_k), g_k = -tau*logsumexp_i(-C_ik/tau + f_i) + tau*log(u_k/B); P from the normalised potentials; repair the column sums to u_k/B by largest remainder; c_ihat = argmax_k P_ik with ties by cost then code id; vbar_i = sum_k P_ik v_k; z_q = z_i + (v_{c_ihat} - z_i).detach() + (vbar_i - vbar_i.detach()); r_i^{l+1} = z_i^l - v_{c_ihat}. The loss is unchanged from the RQ-VAE baseline (reconstruction plus commitment); no new loss term and no new parameter.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: inputs are the per-level residual batch z_i^l (B x d), the codebook V_l (K x d), the top-20 training successor lists S(i), the detached Euclidean code table euc_l(.) over all training items, and the detached scalars (c_l, s_l, tau). Outputs are a code c_ihat in 1..K per item, the quantized vector z_q, the next residual r_i^{l+1}, and the plan P used for the straight-through gradient.
SAFEGUARDS: psi maps into radius 0.95/sqrt(c_l) so sqrt(c_ik)*||.|| <= 0.95 < 1 always; the artanh argument is clamped to 1-1e-6; the Möbius denominator is clamped to 1e-12; Sinkhorn runs in the log domain for 10 iterations with largest-remainder repair of the column sums; tau is clamped; ties are broken deterministically; sigma_l is floored at 1e-6 and delta_l is set to 0 if the null is degenerate; c_l is clamped to [0.25, 4.0]; codes with u_k = 0 are excluded from the plan exactly as in the Euclidean pass; s_l falls back to the previous step's value if the batch is degenerate; the per-level usage-multiset equality is asserted and logged. Four-rank safety: the curvature profile is produced offline and read from a file by every rank; the Euclidean code table is recomputed identically on every rank from the replicated codebook after the DDP step; any gather is an equal-shape all_gather on all ranks; there is no rank-0-only broadcast or export inside the training loop.
END IDEA
